headline: NEWMONT Q2: REVENUE $6.12B, RECORD $2.2B FREE CASH FLOW — EPS $2.06; Cadia Offline, Full-Year Guidance Intact (NYSE: NEM)
snippet: Newmont Corporation reported July 23 that Q2 2026 revenue reached $6.12 billion (up 15.1% year-over-year) with diluted EPS of $2.06 and record second-quarter free cash flow of $2.2 billion, driven by higher realized gold and silver prices that more than offset lower volumes at some sites — including the Cadia underground operation in Australia, offline since an April 14 seismic event with a phased restart underway and full ramp expected in Q3 2026. The world's largest gold producer maintained its full-year guidance of 5.6–5.9 million gold ounces and produced 1.3 million ounces of gold, 17,000 tonnes of copper, and 7 million ounces of silver in the quarter.

headline: $18.5B EQUINOX-ORLA MERGER CLEARS BOTH VOTES — 99.83% For; Court July 28, Close July 31 (TSX: EQX / ORQ)
snippet: Equinox Gold and Orla Mining securityholders both voted to approve their business combination on July 22, with 99.83% of Equinox votes cast in favour of issuing up to 421.8 million new shares — one Equinox share per Orla share plus US$0.0001 cash — valuing the combined entity at approximately US$18.5 billion. A final order from the Supreme Court of British Columbia is expected around July 28, with deal closing anticipated July 31, creating one of Canada's largest multi-jurisdiction gold producers with operations spanning Mexico, Brazil, Canada, and the United States.

headline: GROUP ELEVEN STONEPARK: 21.7% Zn+Pb IN 550m STEP-OUT — Biggest Resource-Growth Hit Since 2017 in Ireland (TSXV: ZNG)
snippet: Group Eleven Resources Corp. (TSXV: ZNG) announced July 23 that a new and robust zone of mineralization has been discovered at its 78.62%-owned Stonepark zinc-lead project in Ireland — step-out hole 26-2638-07 intersecting 14.7 metres grading 2.0% Zn+Pb from 461 metres depth including 2.8 metres at 8.3% Zn+Pb and 1.0 metre at 21.7% Zn+Pb with 4 g/t Ag, located 550 metres from the nearest edge of the existing MRE. The company called it its most significant Stonepark progress since 2017, materially expanding the district footprint 20 kilometres northwest of the Ballywire discovery — a step-out that demonstrates open resource growth potential in one of Europe's most productive zinc districts.

headline: NTH CYCLE TO LIST ON NYSE AT $585M — First U.S. Critical Mineral Recycler + $1.1B Trafigura Off-take (Ticker: NTH)
snippet: Nth Cycle Inc. and Kensington Capital Acquisition Corp. VI announced July 22 a definitive $585-million SPAC combination to list Nth Cycle on NYSE under the ticker NTH, closing expected Q4 2026 — the company operates the first U.S. refinery to produce high-purity nickel-cobalt mixed hydroxide product from recycled battery scrap, using its proprietary OYSTER electro-extraction system that also processes mined copper and rare earth feedstocks. The deal is underpinned by a 10-year off-take term sheet with Trafigura valued at approximately $1.1 billion, positioning Nth Cycle as the only pure-play critical mineral refiner building a U.S.-domestic battery-metals supply chain outside Chinese control.

headline: GREENLIGHT METALS BEND: 52m AT 1.12 g/t Au; FAST-41 FEDERAL MILESTONE — Wisconsin VMS Extends Down-Dip 75m (TSXV: GRL)
snippet: GreenLight Metals Inc. (TSXV: GRL) announced July 23 that drill hole B26-009W returned 52.18 metres of broad gold-bearing mineralization at 1.12 g/t Au (1.28% CuEq) including 10.82 metres at 2.49 g/t Au at its Bend copper-gold VMS deposit in Taylor County, Wisconsin — extending the down-dip footprint approximately 75 metres from the 2025 discovery, while hole B26-011 returned a copper-rich interval of 10.07 metres at 0.96% Cu and 1.09 g/t Au. The company simultaneously announced it achieved a FAST-41 federal permitting milestone that streamlines the regulatory pathway for what could become the first new VMS mine permitted in Wisconsin in decades.

headline: LAHONTAN GOLD CALVADA: 31m AT 0.90 g/t Au OXIDE FROM GEOTECHNICAL HOLE — Nevada Santa Fe Mine Targets 2027 Construction (TSXV: LG)
snippet: Lahontan Gold Corp. (TSXV: LG) disclosed July 22 that a geotechnical drill hole sunk at Calvada Central for mine-permitting purposes at its Santa Fe Mine Project in Nevada unexpectedly returned 30.8 metres grading 0.93 g/t Au Eq oxide — including 10.7 metres at 2.18 g/t Au Eq — ranking among the highest-grade intercepts drilled to date within the Central Calvada deposit. The economic oxide hit reinforces the project's heap-leach potential and supports the company's confidence in advancing toward a targeted 2027 construction start at a permitted Nevada gold asset where the geotechnical program is now delivering exploration upside as a side effect.

headline: SAGA METALS RADAR: 244m OXIDE INTERCEPT, 53% Fe2O3, 7.7% TiO2 — Labrador Ti-V MRE Now 67 Holes (TSXV: SAGA)
snippet: SAGA Metals Corp. (TSXV: SAGA) released July 22 the latest assays from its 100%-owned Radar Titanium-Vanadium-Iron Project in Labrador — holes R-0050 to R-0054 returning intercepts of 53.07% Fe2O3, 7.68% TiO2, and 0.384% V2O5, adding to a maiden MRE program now spanning 67 completed holes with the best hole returning 244.4 metres of continuous semi-massive oxide. Radar covers the entire 160 km² Dykes River layered mafic intrusion and is being advanced as a strategic North American source of titanium and vanadium — both now classified as critical under U.S. and Canadian policy — with a resource estimate in progress.

headline: CHINA'S RARE EARTH BAN 'BACKFIRED' PER CSIS — 55 Nations Cooperating; But Japan Got 4% of Dysprosium Quota, Germany Got None
snippet: CSIS critical minerals security program head Gracelin Baskaran argued in a Mining.com analysis published July 21 that Beijing's decision to restrict seven heavy rare earth elements — including dysprosium and terbium — has unintentionally accelerated the international cooperation that could weaken China's stranglehold, pointing to a 55-country U.S. State Department ministerial as the largest critical minerals meeting ever convened. Despite the diplomatic momentum, the data remains stark: heavy rare earth shipments are still down 50% from pre-restriction levels, Japan received just 4% of its prior dysprosium imports, and Germany received none — supply disruptions that are forcing aerospace and defence manufacturers into spot markets with no guarantee of availability.

headline: RARE EARTH MARKET JULY: NdPr AT 2026 HIGH $133/KG, MOFCOM BLACKLISTS MP MATERIALS — 18 of 18 Elements Rise, Germanium +27.8%
snippet: Main Rich International's July 2026 rare earth market update documents a sweeping price advance — all 18 tracked rare earth elements posted gains this month, led by germanium (+27.8%), dysprosium (+25.4%), and indium (+26.5%), with NdPr oxide printing a 2026 high of approximately $133/kg after troughing at $90/kg in early June. On June 22, MOFCOM added MP Materials and USA Rare Earth to its entity list — barring anyone worldwide from supplying them Chinese-origin rare earth materials — while outside China, heavy rare earths like dysprosium and terbium are now described as effectively unavailable at any price, bifurcating global markets into separate Chinese and non-Chinese pricing structures.

headline: GDX TOP 25 ON TRACK FOR SECOND-BEST QUARTER EVER — 50% YoY Unit Profit Surge as Q2 Earnings Season Opens
snippet: An Investing.com analysis ahead of the gold mining sector's Q2 2026 earnings season argues that the GDX top 25 producers are on track to report their second-best quarter on record — projected unit profits (gold price minus all-in sustaining costs) expected to surge 50% year-over-year — yet the gains may paradoxically widen the valuation disconnect between mining equities and bullion rather than close it. With gold correcting 28% from its January peak while miners remain highly profitable at $4,000, the piece frames a central question for H2 2026: does the market re-rate mining equities upward to reflect near-record profitability, or does bullion's correction eventually drag equity prices lower despite the fundamentals?
